item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E001","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"In its 31 March 2023 report, the GIEI described agreements with Mexican authorities, COVAJ and UEILCA concerning activation of existing arrest warrants, investigations into authorship, obstruction and torture, access to prisons and proceedings, and targeted information from Sedena and Semar; it stated that a new agreement was expected to extend the GIEI mandate to June 2023.","notes":["The excerpt describes a planned new agreement extending the mandate, not a completed extension."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E003","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The GIEI reported that investigative progress was obstructed by falsification or concealment of information, torture-tainted self-incriminations, withdrawn arrest warrants, pressure on the special prosecutor and team turnover, with continuing delays; it recognized significant advances by Fiscal Omar Gómez and his team and reported that Sedena and Marina denied information that the GIEI had documented.","notes":["The excerpt does not support the broader claim that Marina concealed secret operations and torture or that it later cooperated."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E004","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E005","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E006","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The Mexican president inaugurated a centralized 40,000-square-meter medicine warehouse intended to supply hospitals nationwide, with delivery by the armed forces or Birmex within 24–48 hours; AP reported severe medication-access problems, including unfilled prescriptions rising from 1.5 million in 2019 to 22 million in 2021 and about 12.5 million in 2022, while experts questioned the logistics and risks of centralization.","notes":["The supplied excerpt does not state the inauguration date of 29 December 2023."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E007","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"CONEVAL reported producing multidimensional poverty and social-rights indicators, coordinating and concluding 173 evaluations in 2023, publishing monitoring and evaluation products, and analyzing health access and women’s rights; it reported 2,011 identified uses of its information during January 2023–June 2024 and a 34.4% increase over the 2012–2022 average.","notes":["The excerpt does not support the figure of 1,218 uses in 2023 alone."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E009","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E010","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E011","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"BTI reports that the AMLO government created commissions concerning historical crimes and the Ayotzinapa disappearances but blocked initiatives seeking army information, refused to meet with a prominent victims’ movement leader, cut resources for victims’ organizations, changed the methodology for counting disappeared persons to lower the official number, and was ineffective in investigating more than 100,000 reported missing people.","notes":["The supplied excerpt does not support the added wording about public commitments or institutional cooperation."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E012","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"BTI 2024 reports that AMLO expanded military involvement in internal security and economic activities despite campaign promises to reduce it; cartel influence, high homicide levels and impunity persisted; Plan B was intended to weaken electoral oversight; the president attacked journalists and autonomous organizations; and pressure was placed on the Supreme Court’s independence.","notes":["The supplied excerpt describes legal challenges to Plan B and the National Guard transfer as pending; it does not contain the later invalidation decisions."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E013","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E014","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The 2023 CCC Index ranked Mexico 12th, with an overall score of 3.87 versus 4.05 in 2022 and a fourth consecutive annual decline; it reported adverse conditions for journalists and civil society, AMLO’s criticism of journalists and independent agencies, allegations of Pegasus surveillance, an INAI quorum crisis after his vetoes, and institutional shortcomings hindering corruption-case resolution, while noting a 2023 anti-corruption budget increase and a Segalmex investigation.","notes":["The excerpt states Mexico’s rank as 12 but does not state that it was 12th of 15 countries."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E015","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E016","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E017","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
